scope: The PRE marginal is unobserved in this release and is SWEPT, never assumed. The design effect uses an ICC estimated from rater-level positive-share dispersion in the released POST data; a PRE arm's clustering could differ and nothing here measures it. This round estimates a floor and tests no hypothesis.
verdict: B BASELINE-ELEVATED. The POST arm's sign marginal is measured, not assumed: 0.7701 positive over 102,146 released ratings, with the neutral point used 1 time(s). If the PRE arm shares that marginal, chance agreement is 0.6459 -- NOT 0.5 -- leaving 0.3541 of room above it, so a naive test against 0.5 would report agreement far above chance while measuring nothing but the shared tendency to write positive criteria. Rater clustering is real: 1108 raters with >=10 ratings have positive-shares of median 0.760 [0.686, 0.878], giving ICC 0.0915 and a design effect of 1.37 at the PLANNED 5 criteria per participant -- note the release's own 92 ratings per rater would give 9.32, which is not this experiment's cluster size -- so the effective n is roughly n/1.37, not n. At 400 matched criterion pairs the minimum detectable departure is 0.0548; reaching 0.02 needs about 3,001 pairs. THE PRE MARGINAL IS UNOBSERVED BY ANYONE -- no participant in this release wrote a criterion before seeing responses, which is why S_pre needs an experiment at all -- so it is swept across 0.50-0.95 and every figure here is conditional on the swept value, with the tightest room across that sweep being 0.2569.
